Source: On exam, the patient is an obese girl who is clutching her head with the light in the room turned off.
Her temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 123/74 mmHg, pulse is 85/min, and respirations are 13/min.
A lumbar puncture reveals an increased opening pressure with a normal glucose level.
Fundoscopic exam reveals mild bilateral papilledema.
There has been a recent outbreak of measles at the patient’s school and the patient’s mother has been trying to give her daughter medicine to prevent her from getting sick.
The patient has had headaches in the past but this is the worst headache of her life.
The patient states that the pain is mostly on the left side of her head.
Her neurological exam is within normal limits.
An MRI of the head is obtained and reveals cerebral edema.
Her mother fears that her daughter may have caught measles.
A 17-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with a headache.
Her symptoms started yesterday and have been getting progressively worse.
